gates.rationale: Keeps the package manager, overrides, and lockfile dependency policy pinned.
Keeps native install scripts limited to the reviewed workspace allowlist.
Requires explicit review evidence before a lockfile change is accepted.
Keeps every workflow job time-boxed, pull_request workflows cancel superseded runs, actions on Node24 majors, and no redundant core build (operations-hygiene runbook §CI).

Keeps deterministic pipeline output snapshots stable in every validation scope. Resource isolation avoids overlapping baseline compiler/input scans with other CPU-heavy gates; an isolated diagnostic completed in 62s with natural exit and no retained handle. The exact failed-runner exit delay remains unattributed. Selection and the 120s timeout are unchanged.

Runs the pr-deterministic scenario suite (eval/scenarios, simulated and model-free) so fixture-served pipelines, approval gates and fail-closed unstubbed ops keep their contract; same as pnpm scenario run eval/scenarios --lane pr-deterministic.
Runs the deterministic QM-03 V-layer notebook fold and consolidation benchmark in the governed check lane.
Prevents shared JSON and schema construction helpers from regressing into local implementations.
Fails closed when a governed catalog silently falls back instead of loading its validated source.
Prevents type-safety debt from increasing.

Prevents import cycles and layer direction debt from increasing. Resource isolation prevents this repository-wide graph scan from competing with other gates after it reached the unchanged 120s deadline in a concurrent full run; contention is a mitigation hypothesis, not a uniquely confirmed cause.
Prevents new production modules from exceeding the 1,500-line simplicity boundary.
Ratchets the published subpath count of each libs/* package (the @agent/core public surface) so it can only shrink unless a change raises the baseline in review.

Ratchets how many core modules secure-io, path-resolver, logger and every foundation/contracts module pull in at runtime (measured on libs/core/dist), so domain rules cannot silently make the base layer heavier.

Keeps store custody and role coverage aligned, validates every state/ledger/floor registration and its effective retention-policy reference, preserves partition binding, and ratchets unscoped-legacy stores down.
Keeps static foundation state/ledger/floor roots projected from validated catalog registrations without runtime catalog I/O.
Keeps docs/developer/architecture/dependency-graph.mmd generated from the workspace package manifests so the package layering diagram cannot go stale.
Keeps the first-win command contract and documentation fences aligned.
Prevents internal exception details from being projected onto network-facing responses.
Keeps the single CLI entrypoint and command ownership map valid.
Keeps the public entry documents understandable without internal runtime terms.
Keeps improvement plans searchable and prevents a second undocumented status source.
Keeps status, concept, and onboarding documentation anchored to one explicit source map.

One registered definition, canonical doc and glossary entry per high-confusion term; retired docs carry doc_status + superseded_by and never stay canonical; new architecture docs map onto registered concepts; every monthly plan is indexed.
Rejects broken relative Markdown links before they become unreachable documentation.
Rejects documented pnpm/kyberion commands that do not exist, unlisted pipelines, a stale COMPONENT_MAP, and a stale generated docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md (links are covered by documentation-links).
Keeps all text bridges on the shared turn/thread/typing lifecycle.
Fails when source references an active/shared/runtime/<name> store with no storage-retention-catalog entry, so new ledgers and runtime dirs cannot grow unbounded and invisible to the janitor.
Keeps manifest scopes connected to the PR, full, and release workflow entrypoints.
Keeps actuator operations covered by preflight contracts.
Requires every discovered actuator operation to publish an input schema and example.
Checks every schema-bound pipeline invocation after template resolution and keeps inferred legacy operations open during migration.
Keeps extension registration deterministic and dependency-safe.
Checks declared module invariants after the build.
Prevents new duplicate capability seams.
Checks capability seam registry coverage.

Checks capability seam adoption at the AST boundary. Resource isolation prevents this repository-wide TypeScript scan from competing with other gates after it reached the unchanged 120s deadline in a concurrent full run; contention is a mitigation hypothesis, not a uniquely confirmed cause.

Keeps forge access on the vcs-host seam: production code may not exec the gh CLI outside the allowlisted provider/diagnostic files, nor reference the deprecated sync gh verbs of libs/core/vcs/github.ts (VCS host API seam design, stage 5).

Computes the call-level role assumption reachability report in memory (RN-02; not committed) and fails only on RN-03 invariant violations: role-assumption-policy.json must grant every reachable role, govern exactly the analysed system roles and every SYSTEM_ROLE a package script launches, narrowed system roles must stay fully resolved, and no system role may gain unresolved (any role) sites or SYSTEM_ROLE-inheriting child-process entries beyond its counts in role-assumption-unresolved-baseline (a count below its baseline only warns to lower it).json (counts only). `--write-report` writes the report to active/shared/cache/system/role-assumption/ for review. Budget: it type-checks scripts/, libs/core/ and libs/actuators/ as one TypeScript program (about 32s CPU, 40-50s wall alone on a loaded 4-vCPU host, 2-3x that while `pnpm check` runs 6 gates at once), so the 120s default timed out on busy runs.
Keeps reasoning provider declarations aligned with the runtime registry.
Checks package and artifact contracts after the build.
Ensures declared script and pipeline references resolve on every built PR and full validation run.
Checks runtime ESM integrity.

Keeps one @agent/core instance per process: production code outside libs/core imports it by package name, never by a relative path into libs/core, except the listed build/clean bootstrap files (a second instance duplicates module-private grant registries).

Catches dist/presence, dist/satellites, and dist/scripts entry points whose bare imports resolve fine at typecheck time (via tsconfig paths, or a source package's own local node_modules) but are never linked into the shared root node_modules the compiled flat dist tree actually resolves from, so `node <entry>` fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND at process startup. Covers both workspace-package imports (e.g. nexus-daemon and @actuator/service) and third-party imports declared as a real dependency somewhere in the repo (e.g. discord-bridge and discord.js).

Checks catalog and knowledge index integrity. Resource isolation reduces contention during repository-wide catalog, vocabulary and knowledge-index scans after a concurrent full run increased from 114s to the unchanged 120s deadline; the exact timeout cause remains unattributed.

Checks intent domain coverage.
Checks contract schema coverage and validity.
Checks generated PII rules.
Runs the deterministic distill evaluation.
Checks actuator contract semver compatibility on every PR so manifest/schema bumps cannot skip rebaseline.
Checks portable pipeline shell usage.
Checks workflow catalog references.
Checks process definition registry bindings.
Checks mission process bindings.
Checks reference drift contracts.
Surfaces production evidence readiness without blocking local validation.
Checks the production evidence register contract.
Checks first-win smoke contract.
Checks first-win lifecycle dry-run.
Checks tagged documentation examples.
Checks tier hygiene boundaries.
Checks enumerated operator mutation boundaries, scoped administrator selection settings, and mandatory hosted Chromium selection flows in CI (explicit local browser skip is not validation).
Checks audit continuity in warn-only observation mode.

Prevents release promotion until external production evidence is complete.

TC-11: fails when the agent pool cannot supply a role the obligations catalog can require or a mission-team template declares required, and when a hard separation-of-duties pair can never be independent. Team roles and agent profiles declared capabilities that were never compared, so an uncoverable role was still filled by the least-bad candidate.

TC-17: fails when a declared backend utility_fit claim is contradicted by a recorded role-fitness probe, or when the governed reasoning-backend policy allows a mode no capability profile describes. Every CLI and API backend claims judge/divergent capability by default argument and nothing checked it.

OW-07: fails when a new orphan appears — an unimported libs/core module, an uninvoked script, an unreachable pipeline or an unreferenced actuator op; known exceptions are reasoned baseline entries that may only shrink.
Fails on runtime import cycles; type-only and intentional lazy-import edges are allowed. Keeps the domain split from regrowing load-order hazards.
SC-02: every manifest capability must declare its side-effect class (read/write/egress/none) so preflight can classify ops.

S3: registration-ceremony ratchets (storage/IO/process/package boundaries, R5 delegation start reporting per reasoning backend, tenant-partitioned runtime stores reachable by offboarding, loopback child-env NO_PROXY guard, typed provider results redacted fail-closed, non-public reasoning payload scopes declaring training_use) and seam lifecycle/provider-boundary contracts, including OCR removal cache invalidation. Budget: about 30s wall alone; scanning under six concurrent gates uses a 60s test timeout and 300s gate timeout. tests/core-runtime-import-contract.test.ts stays in the test job.

S6: real-time sleeps in test files (setTimeout(resolve, N), sleep(N)) may only decrease; they race TTLs, deadlines and background work on loaded CI runners. Use fake timers, vi.waitFor or an injected clock instead.

MSN-STORE-BOUNDS-2 P1: whole-file reads of append-only JSONL stores (readJsonLines, readJsonLinesCached, safeReadFile(...).split('\n') in .jsonl files) may only decrease per file; past the 100MB read cap they make every read throw. Use the purpose readers in libs/core/storage/jsonl-read.ts instead.
